blockers.description: trySetName in may-core.js (line 176) hardcodes savedData.synthetic = true unconditionally. A real pre-production learner enrolled via the normal flow would be marked synthetic:true even though they are a real person.
blockers.mitigation: Acceptable for pilot if: (a) learner is informed the synthetic marker is incorrect, (b) the pilot is consent-based, (c) the marker can be corrected post-hoc by editing localStorage or adding a consent flag. For production: add a parameter to trySetName that respects a consent/real-user flag.
blockers.impacts: Export payloads will have synthetic:true for a real user — could confuse analytics if exports are compared between synthetic and real learners.

blockers.description: Student roll row divs (.may-student-row) lack tabIndex and onkeydown (Enter/Space) handlers. Keyboard-only users cannot navigate and select from the roll.
blockers.mitigation: Deferred post-pilot polish. Mouse/touch interaction is sufficient for a single-user pilot. Add tabIndex='0' and keyboard handlers in a follow-up session.
blockers.impacts: Screen-reader and keyboard-only users cannot use the student roll UI.

prerequisites: Human explicitly approves single-user local pre-production pilot
Learner is informed this is a pre-production version with known gaps
Learner consents to local-only data storage (no cloud, no external telemetry)
Exam date and goals entered voluntarily by learner — system never pulls from external sources
Data export capability explained to learner (exportMayPilotData preserves their practice history)
No external telemetry endpoint may be added without explicit authorization
The synthetic:true marker on a real-learner profile is acknowledged as a known gap
summary: 24 checklist items assessed. 23 PASS, 1 PASS_WITH_NOTE (PILOT-07). 2 blockers: 1 MEDIUM (synthetic marker), 1 LOW (keyboard nav). All safety/recommendation/evidence/exam-plan/privacy systems confirmed intact and tested at 248/248. May is functionally ready for a controlled single-user pilot. The BLOCK-01 synthetic marker issue is acceptable for a consent-based pre-production pilot.
